event: Indus Valley civilization; seals showing seated figures (e.g. the 'Pashupati' seal) are speculatively read as proto-yoga
significance: Evidence is contested; most scholars treat any yoga link as unproven

event: Composition of the Ṛgveda; √yuj appears in the sense of yoking (chariots; later the mind) alongside ecstatic seer figures (kesin; muni)
significance: Earliest vocabulary layer of the tradition; no systematic yoga yet

event: Atharvaveda compiled; hymns on prāṇa (vital breath) and the ritual ascetic vrātyas
significance: Early breath and asceticism ideas that later feed prāṇāyāma and tapas

event: Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas interiorize ritual; tapas (heat; austerity) and breath control become central practices
significance: Shift from external sacrifice to internal discipline

short_title: Early prose Upaniṣads: ātman-brahman and inner sacrifice
event: Early prose Upaniṣads teach ātman-brahman identity and meditation as inner sacrifice
significance: Philosophical ground for later yoga goals (liberation through knowledge)

event: Kaṭha Upaniṣad gives an early definition of yoga as firm holding of the senses (chariot metaphor)
significance: First strong use of 'yoga' as a discipline of mind and senses

event: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad gives early instructions on posture and breath within a devotional (Rudra-Śiva) frame
significance: Early mention of body alignment and breath in meditation

event: Maitrī Upaniṣad describes a six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) yoga
significance: Precursor to Patañjali's eight limbs

short_title: Śramaṇa movements: the Buddha and Mahāvīra
event: Śramaṇa movements: the Buddha and Mahāvīra teach meditation (dhyāna) and ascetic discipline outside Vedic orthodoxy
significance: Parallel meditation systems; mutual influence with Patañjali is debated

event: Mahābhārata includes the Bhagavad Gītā (karma- jñāna- and bhakti-yoga; yoga as equanimity) and Sāṃkhya-Yoga material in the Mokṣadharma
significance: Yoga becomes a broad path concept beyond meditation (Gītā 2.48 samatvaṃ yoga ucyate)

event: Patañjali's Yoga Sūtras compiled (~195 sūtras in four pādas); eight-limbed (aṣṭāṅga) path; Sāṃkhya metaphysics
significance: Foundational classical yoga text; teaches a steady seat for meditation rather than a posture repertoire (YS 2.46)

event: Īśvarakṛṣṇa's Sāṃkhyakārikā systematizes the 25 tattvas and the three guṇas
significance: Standard source for the puruṣa-prakṛti-guṇa framework

event: Vyāsa's Yoga Bhāṣya becomes the standard commentary on the Yoga Sūtras
significance: Earliest extant commentary; Sūtras and Bhāṣya may have circulated as one work

event: Vācaspati Miśra writes the Tattvavaiśāradī sub-commentary on the Yoga Bhāṣya
significance: Major interpretive layer for later Yoga-Sāṃkhya scholarship

event: Tantric traditions elaborate mantra; mudrā; cakras; nāḍīs and kuṇḍalinī; Kashmir Śaivism develops
significance: Subtle-body models later absorbed into haṭha yoga

event: Nāth Siddha ascetics develop haṭha yoga techniques (bandhas; mudrās; breath retention) aimed at stabilizing bindu and breath; very few āsanas taught
significance: Origin of haṭha practice; posture is a minor limb

event: Svātmārāma compiles the Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā; teaches 15 āsanas plus ṣaṭkarma; prāṇāyāma; mudrā; samādhi
significance: Most influential premodern haṭha manual

short_title: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists
event: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā (32 āsanas); Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā (1737; 84 āsanas)
texts: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā; Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā
significance: Posture repertoire grows but stays mostly seated and floor-based

event: Theosophical Society founded (1875); Orientalist translations and Western esotericism recast yoga; haṭha yogis often dismissed as 'fakirs' by reformers
significance: Sets conditions for the modern reframing of yoga

event: Swami Vivekananda at the Parliament of the World's Religions (Chicago 1893); Rāja Yoga published 1896 reframes Patañjali for a Western audience
significance: Starts modern transnational yoga; emphasizes meditation over postures

short_title: Physical culture meets yoga; modern postural yoga forms
event: Indian physical culture merges with European gymnastics and YMCA-style fitness; modern postural yoga takes shape
key_figures: Bishnu Charan Ghosh; Shri Yogendra; Swami Kuvalayananda
significance: Scholars (Singleton; Alter) describe modern posture practice as a hybrid

event: Shri Yogendra founds The Yoga Institute in Bombay (Santa Cruz); visits the US in 1919
significance: Begins institutional householder yoga in India

short_title: Yogananda arrives in the US; SRF founded
event: Paramahansa Yogananda arrives in the US and founds Self-Realization Fellowship; Kriya Yoga reaches the West
significance: Early large-scale Indian yoga teaching in America

event: Swami Kuvalayananda founds Kaivalyadhama (Lonavla) and the journal Yoga Mīmāṃsā; laboratory research on yoga
significance: Start of scientific yoga research

event: Krishnamacharya teaches in the Mysore Palace yogaśālā under the Maharaja; publishes Yoga Makaranda (1934); dynamic vinyāsa sequences emerge
significance: Root of the Ashtanga; Iyengar and Viniyoga lines

event: Swami Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh
significance: Source of the Sivananda lineage (Vishnudevananda; Satchidananda; Satyananda)

event: Autobiography of a Yogi published
significance: Brings yoga and Kriya to a mass Western readership

short_title: Indra Devi in Hollywood; Jois's institute in Mysore
event: Indra Devi opens a yoga studio in Hollywood (1947); K. Pattabhi Jois founds the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute in Mysore (1948)
significance: Yoga reaches celebrity circles; Ashtanga formally institutionalized

short_title: Menuhin brings Iyengar to the West
event: Yehudi Menuhin meets B.K.S. Iyengar (1952) and brings him to the West (1954)
significance: Iyengar's international teaching begins

event: Swami Vishnudevananda opens the first Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre (Montréal)
significance: Spreads Sivananda Yoga across North America

event: Television yoga: Richard Hittleman's Yoga for Health (from 1961) and Lilias Folan's Lilias; Yoga and You (from c. 1970)
significance: Mass-market home yoga in the US

short_title: Light on Yoga published; Integral Yoga Institute NYC
event: B.K.S. Iyengar's Light on Yoga published; Swami Satchidananda opens the Integral Yoga Institute in New York
significance: Defining reference for modern āsana practice

event: Counterculture era: Beatles visit Maharishi in Rishikesh (1968); Satchidananda opens Woodstock (1969); Yogi Bhajan founds 3HO (1969)
key_figures: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi; Swami Satchidananda; Yogi Bhajan
significance: Yoga becomes a mainstream Western spiritual and wellness movement

short_title: Institutions consolidate (Himalayan Institute, Pune, Yoga Journal)
event: Himalayan Institute founded (1971); Iyengar institute in Pune opens (1975); Pattabhi Jois first teaches in the US (1975); Yoga Journal founded (1975)
key_figures: Swami Rama; B.K.S. Iyengar; K. Pattabhi Jois
significance: Institutions and publishing consolidate the Western scene

event: Bikram Choudhury opens a studio in Beverly Hills (heated 26-posture sequence)
significance: Origin of branded hot yoga

event: T.K.V. Desikachar founds Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai
significance: Individualized therapeutic Viniyoga lineage

event: Studio-yoga boom: Jivamukti (1984); Power Yoga (1995); Anusara (1997); Yoga Alliance (1999)
key_figures: Sharon Gannon; David Life; Beryl Bender Birch; John Friend
significance: Vinyasa and hybrid styles go mainstream in the US

event: Critical history of modern yoga: De Michelis's A History of Modern Yoga (2004); Alter's Yoga in Modern India (2004); Singleton's Yoga Body (2010)
key_figures: Elizabeth De Michelis; Joseph Alter; Mark Singleton
texts: A History of Modern Yoga; Yoga in Modern India; Yoga Body
significance: Reframes modern postural yoga as a twentieth-century hybrid

event: United Nations proclaims 21 June International Day of Yoga (Dec 2014); first observed 2015
significance: Global institutional recognition

event: Teacher-misconduct reckonings (e.g. Bikram; Anusara; Ashtanga; 3HO); decolonization and appropriation debates; trauma-informed yoga and yoga therapy grow
significance: Ethics and inclusion now part of many trainings; verify specifics before citing
